column1: "Although swings in net exports have affected the data, recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace." Given inflation remains somewhat elevated and the FOMC held the 4.25–4.5% range while continuing balance-sheet runoff, the tone aligns with a cautiously hawkish inflation-targeting stance: Taylor-rule/New Keynesian prescriptions (Clarida, Galí, and Gertler) and forward-guidance frameworks (Svensson and Woodford) imply keeping policy restrictive when unemployment is low and inflation is above target; setting interest on reserve balances at 4.4% is consistent with the post-2008 floor system. Net: modestly positive growth signal tempered by inflation risk management (inflation-at-risk perspective), so slightly less positive than a pure growth read. sentiment score = 0.22
